subject: Dedicated capacity offer and ramp options — SummitGen
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@summitgen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity outline — SummitGen initial offer

Hi Alicia,

Thanks for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is an initial outline for a dedicated capacity offer tied to the usage profile we discussed (chat-heavy customer support models, peaks 9–11am PST, sustained inference during business hours). Summary below — I kept the language action-oriented so procurement can scan quickly and we can iterate.

TL;DR: three options (Conservative, Balanced, Accelerated) that trade off minimum guaranteed GPUs, burst ceilings, and warm-start credits. Each option includes a 12-week ramp playbook with clear activation triggers so SummitGen can avoid paying for idle capacity while getting predictable throughput when traffic grows.

Key bullets:
- Conservative: 8 min GPUs, up to 16 burstable, 12-week phased activation (start 8, +2 every 3 weeks). Good for predictable cost control.
- Balanced: 16 min GPUs, up to 32 burstable, 8-week ramp (start 12, +4 at week 3, +4 at week 6). Best for steady product launches.
- Accelerated: 32 min GPUs, up to 64 burstable, 4-week aggressive onramp with optional warmup credits for peak events.

Operational notes: prefix KV caching for support prompts, autoscale policy recommendations, fallbacks to quantized model variant to preserve latency SLOs during large bursts. SLA: 99.95% availability with failover to hosted pool for non-critical traffic.

Attaching a short worksheet with the activation triggers and expected burn by week. If you want, we can turn one of these into a draft for procurement and DocuSign.

Next steps: if procurement needs an explicit minimum-GPU clause or a ramp-escape hatch, call it out and we’ll bake it into the contract language.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SummitGen_Dedicated_Offer_V2.pdf (PDF, 18 pages), onramp-worksheet-summitgen.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@summitgen.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Shah <raj.shah@summitgen.com>, SummitGen Procurement <procurement@summitgen.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity outline — SummitGen initial offer

Mateo,

Thanks — this is a helpful starting point. A couple of clarifying asks from procurement and our infra team before we share internally:

1) Minimum GPUs: we need clarity on how "min GPUs" maps to concurrency and sustained qps for our average prompt lengths (~300 tokens). Can you include throughput anchors?
2) Ramp schedule: can you add an option that has a longer tail (16 weeks) but with lower initial commitment (4 GPUs) and more frequent small steps — some of our teams prefer gradual ramps to avoid upfront spend.
3) Billing: we prefer month-in-arrears billing with a 30-day termination notice tied to a step-down schedule. Is that supported?

Also cc'ing Raj from procurement to coordinate redlines. If you can send a slightly expanded worksheet showing qps anchors and a 16-week long-tail option, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Product Ops
SummitGen

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SummitGen asks — throughput anchors + long-tail option (internal)

Marissa / Ben / Sofia — forwarding Alicia's asks. Quick internal recommended answers below so we present a single, crisp update:

- Throughput anchors: 300-token avg -> estimated sustained QPS per GPU (nv4-class) = ~5 qps sustained; burst-ready concurrency ~10 qps with batching and KV caching. We'll include a table in the worksheet: GPUs -> sustained qps -> 95th pct p99 latency expectations.
- Long-tail option: propose a 16-week gradual onramp: start 4 GPUs, +2 GPUs every 2 weeks until reaching 22 GPUs (final floor 22) OR allow a soft-floor where after week 12 the floor becomes 12 GPUs unless SummitGen exercises scale-up. Include step-down graceband (30/60/90 day decommit windows) to match procurement's termination cadence.
- Billing: Redwood supports month-in-arrears billing for Dedicated; termination with step-down windows is standard (need procurement sign-off on credits for early decommit).

Action items: Sofia, can you assemble the throughput anchor table & add recommended autoscale policy names? Marissa/Ben, should I attach a plain-language clause describing the step-down/crediting structure, or do you want legal to craft?

I'll draft the updated worksheet and send to Alicia + Raj next week.

-Mateo

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@summitgen.com>, Raj Shah <raj.shah@summitgen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: SummitGen — Updated dedicated commitment options and throughput anchors (v2)

Alicia/Raj,

Per Alicia's notes, attaching an updated offer and an expanded onramp worksheet. Summary of the new options (full tables in the attached PDF and XLSX):

Option A — Long Tail (cost-minimizing)
- Initial floor: 4 GPUs
- Ramp: +2 GPUs every 2 weeks for 16 weeks -> target floor 22 GPUs
- Burstable ceiling: up to 44 GPUs via reserved burst and scheduled event credits
- Throughput anchor: 1 GPU ~ 5 sustained QPS @300 tokens -> conservative baseline 4 GPUs = ~20 sustained QPS
- Step-down: 30/60/90-day step-down windows with prorated credits; month-in-arrears billing

Option B — Practical Balance
- Initial floor: 12 GPUs
- Ramp: +4 GPUs at week 3 and week 7 (8-week ramp) -> target floor 20 GPUs
- Burstable ceiling: 40 GPUs
- Throughput anchor: 12 GPUs = ~60 sustained QPS (with caching)

Option C — Rapid Launch
- Initial floor: 32 GPUs
- Ramp: 4-week aggressive onramp to reach full floor; includes 2 weeks of warmup credits for peak events
- Burstable ceiling: 64 GPUs
- Throughput anchor: 32 GPUs = ~160 sustained QPS

Operational items included in all options:
- Autoscale policy suggestions (concurrency-trigger vs latency-trigger) and default cooldowns
- KV prefix caching recommendations and cache TTLs for customer prompts
- Fallback mapping to quantized variant to preserve p99 latency under heavy burst load

We also included a short sample clause for the minimum-GPU definition (how we map tokens/qps to floor measurements) and a decommit credit table.

Next steps: if procurement is happy with the long-tail Option A as a lower-risk entry point, we can convert Option A into a binding addendum and route to DocuSign. Otherwise, tell us which option to convert and we'll prepare the legal exhibit.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SummitGen_Dedicated_Offer_V2.pdf, onramp-worksheet-summitgen.xlsx

Subject: Re: SummitGen — Updated dedicated commitment options and throughput anchors (v2)

Mateo, Alicia,

Appreciate the clear options and the throughput anchors — that table makes it much easier to validate against our perf tests. Procurement reviewed Option A (Long Tail) and thinks that is the right low-risk path forward subject to two items:

1) We need a DocuSign exhibit that includes the 16-week onramp schedule and the step-down graceband. Can Redwood provide a legal exhibit we can sign electronically?
2) We request the first 2 weeks of warmup credits to be applied during the first month rather than at the end of the ramp.

If you can get us a DocuSign-ready exhibit and confirm the warmup credit timing, we can route internally and aim to return an executed copy within 10 business days.

Thanks,
Raj Shah
Procurement Manager
SummitGen
